scope.flow: TokenWrapper.transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 amount) allowance-based token transfer and its Transfer event emission
scope.environment: Ethereum ERC-20 TokenWrapper contract and off-chain consumers of Transfer events (block explorers, wallets, indexers, tax tools, smart-contract integrations)

entities.name: Token holder (from parameter) whose balance is debited
Block explorers, wallets, indexers, tax tools and event-listening contracts

statements.text: A user or contract calls transferFrom to move tokens on behalf of another address using an allowance, with a from token holder, a to recipient and an amount.
The internal _balanceOf accounting is updated correctly so the actual token balances reflect the proper transfer from the token holder to the recipient.
The spender calls transferFrom(from, to, amount) on TokenWrapper.
TokenWrapper emits a Transfer event for the transferFrom operation.
The implementation substitutes msg.sender (the spender) for the from address in the Transfer event emission instead of emitting the token holder whose balance decreases.
Per EIP-20, the Transfer event emitted by transferFrom must use as its from parameter the address of the token holder whose balance decreases.

The emitted Transfer event identifies the transaction initiator (msg.sender, the spender) as the source of the tokens rather than the actual token holder, creating a permanent incorrect record in blockchain history.

Block explorers such as Etherscan and Blockscout parsing the incorrect events display the operator or router contract as the originating address rather than the actual token holder, so users do not see their TokenWrapper transfers in their sent transactions list.

Wallet applications including MetaMask, Rainbow and Coinbase Wallet populate user transaction histories and portfolio tracking from the incorrect events, so users do not see accurate representations of their TokenWrapper activity.

Off-chain indexing systems such as The Graph subgraphs and Dune Analytics dashboards store and attribute transfers to router contracts and operators rather than actual users, and tax reporting tools fail to detect TokenWrapper transfers, potentially causing incomplete tax reporting and compliance issues.

Smart contract integrations listening to Transfer events for accounting, such as DAO treasury tracking, token-gated access controls, referral tracking or rewards distribution, incorrectly credit activity to operator contracts rather than users, breaking composability.
Every single transferFrom call is affected with one hundred percent likelihood, while on-chain balances are not manipulated and no theft of funds is directly enabled.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the caller is unauthorized or permissionless; the spender is described only as a user or contract using an allowance.
The incorrect event attribution is described as occurring on every transferFrom call, but no concrete transaction or observed event log is supplied.
Downstream harms to explorers, wallets, indexers, tax tools and contract integrations are stated as potential ecosystem consequences, not observed incidents.
Report does not specify the exact event signature/argument ordering or whether the to and amount fields are also affected.
